newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore April exports up after five-month fall.
newsitem.headline: Singapore April exports up after five-month fall.

text.p: Singapore's April non-oil domestic exports rose by 5.9 percent year-on-year after five consecutive declines, the Trade Development Board (TDB) said on Tuesday.
The board said the April rise was due mainly to a 13.4 percent jump in domestic exports of semiconductors following five months of declines.
The trade data was much stronger than the market had expected. A Reuters poll of 11 economists on Monday produced an average forecast of a slim 0.5 percent rise in April non-oil domestic exports.

"The figures are much better than expected. The real surprise was from semiconductors. I had expect it to be flat but it rose by 13.4 percent," said Song Seng Wun, regional economist with ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett Asia Securities.
"Overall, the figures were also much higher and it must include some lumpy items, including sales of aircraft," he said.
Singapore Airlines Ltd had earlier announced that it sold a couple of aircraft.
Economists said the pick up in the key electronics sector, which accounts for nearly 60 percent of exports, meant the Singapore economy was on track for a recovery in the second half.
"We are not totally out of the woods yet, but certainly things are looking more hopeful," said Song.
The TDB said in its statement that monthly trade data tended to be volatile.
"It is too early to conclude on the basis of April's figures that the recovery in global electronic demand has begun," the statement said.
It said re-exports rose 11.7 percent in April as a result of stronger demand for electronics and related products. Imports also climbed 2.5 percent due partly to delivery of ships during the month.
Domestic exports to the United States, Singapore's largest trading partner, rose six percent in April after falling 11.4 percent in March.
Exports to other major markets like Malaysia, Hong Kong and the European Union were also higher, but exports to Japan remained weak, registering a decline of 15.6 percent, the TDB said.
